entities.name: PMID:25090267
observations: Human primary study in Clinical and Investigative Medicine (2014) measured β-catenin protein in frozen-shoulder surgical tissue and IGF2 mRNA in fibroblasts derived from frozen-shoulder tissue; both were increased versus rotator-cuff-tear comparators.
The study did not establish increased IGF2 protein or separately measured synovial-tissue levels.

entities.name: Frozen Shoulder Syndrome
observations: In the identified human study, frozen-shoulder tissue showed increased β-catenin protein, and derived primary fibroblasts showed increased IGF2 mRNA, compared with rotator-cuff-tear controls.
No separate human study measuring IGF2 or CTNNB1 specifically in frozen-shoulder synovial tissue was identified in the performed searches.

entities.name: IGF2
observations: IGF2 expression was significantly increased at the mRNA level in primary fibroblasts derived from frozen-shoulder tissue versus rotator-cuff-derived fibroblasts.
The cited study did not measure IGF2 protein.

entities.name: β-catenin
observations: β-catenin protein was significantly increased in frozen-shoulder tissue extracts versus rotator-cuff-tear tissue by Western immunoblotting.
This is direct protein measurement rather than inference from Wnt-pathway involvement.
